newsitem.title: USA: NYS Gov says reaches final pact on rent rules.
newsitem.headline: NYS Gov says reaches final pact on rent rules.

text.p: New York State Gov George Pataki on Thursday said he had reached a final agreement with the state legislature on apartment rent rules, which have proved to be one of the biggest fights of the session.

Pataki said the new rules would reform the 50-year old system while protecting tenants. New York State has about 1.1 million regulated apartments, the vast majority of which are located in New York City.

"I vowed that we would not change the rules in the middle of the game for the millions of tenants who have come to count on rent control. Promises made, promises kept," said Pataki, in prepared remarks.
The Republican governor had proposed letting apartments return to the free market once a tenant moved out or died, a policy called vacancy decontrol, although he never used the term.

Tenant groups and Assembly Speaker Sheldon Silver, D-Manhattan, had refused to back down on the issue, saying it would end the system swiftly. In the end, a compromise was forged that gives landlords a bigger bonus for vacant apartments.
The battle over the rent regulations stalemated progress in other important areas, from reaching a new state budget, which was due on April 1, to welfare reform.

Senate Majority Leader Joseph Bruno, R-Troy, who had fought the hardest to end the present system of rent regulations, in prepared remarks, said: "The governor and legislative leaders said that with the rent regulation issue resolved, they looked forward to addressing the state budget and other pressing issues facing the state."
